title: QuickProvision: local-first SDK sandpit playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for QuickProvision — a lightweight local/cloud sandpit aimed at making the SDK first-run experience predictable and low-friction for engineers evaluating Redwood. The emphasis is on a local-first developer loop that mirrors hosted behavior, surface-level telemetry to measure success, and a small set of deterministic examples that exercise common failure modes.

Scope (what belongs here):
- Minimal local provisioning (docker-compose + small dev VM image) to run a stubbed Redwood runtime and a tiny model shim.
- A reproducible quickstart that takes a dev from git clone -> hello-world inference in <= 10 minutes on mac/linux/windows WSL.
- A checklist for converting the sandpit to an air-gapped/test-only package for POCs.
- Telemetry probes and smoke metrics to determine whether users "completed" the quickstart (not analytics-level, only probe counts).

Non-goals:
- Full parity with Dedicated/Private builds. This is intentionally small and opinionated.
- Production-grade security hardening. Aim for safety-by-configuration, not hardening.

Quick win flows (user Journeys)
1) Zero-install demo (web): user clicks a link -> spins ephemeral sandbox in cloud -> gets a token -> runs sample chat in browser.
2) Local dev loop (recommended): git clone -> quickprovision up -> SDK sample app -> generate -> done.
3) Airgap POC: package quickprovision tar.gz (images + shim) -> run behind customer network -> follow offline onboarding checklist.

Minimum feature checklist for quickprovision up:
- [ ] single binary (or script) that:
  - pulls images (or uses local VM image)
  - starts a stub runtime exposing the same API surface as hosted (POST /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings)
  - provisions a short-lived API token for the local session
- [ ] example SDK app in JS and Python with explicit env var sample (.env.example)
- [ ] smoke tests that validate generate, stream, and a failing request path (400)
- [ ] lightweight telemetry hooks (file-based event log) recording step completions

Quickstart (local, mac/linux):
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickprovision.git
2) cd quickprovision && ./quickprovision init && ./quickprovision up
   - init creates ~/.quickprovision/config with a dev token and default port 8088
   - up starts a local runtime (docker-compose or run containerd image)
3) cd examples/js-hello && npm i && REDWOOD_API_URL=http://localhost:8088 REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat ~/.quickprovision/token) node index.js
4) Expectation: prints a 1–2 sentence generated reply within 2s on a modern laptop.

Example SDK snippet (JS) to include in quickstart page: (kept deliberately tiny)
// index.js
// assume process.env.REDWOOD_API_URL, REDWOOD_API_KEY set
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
async function hello() {
  const res = await fetch(process.env.REDWOOD_API_URL + '/v1/responses', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'quick-demo', input: 'Write a 2-sentence friendly greeting.' })
  });
  const json = await res.json();
  console.log(json.output_text || json.choices?.[0]?.text || JSON.stringify(json));
}
hello().catch(e=>console.error('demo failed', e));

Developer debugging notes (common friction points):
- Port conflicts: default 8088 -> change via QUICKPROVISION_PORT env var. Document how to inspect 'quickprovision logs' and stop processes.
- Token not found: init step stores token in ~/.quickprovision/token (plain file). For security POC we will offer KMS integration later; for now make it visible so users can copy/paste.
- Networking issues on corporate VPNs: recommend switching to the ephemeral web demo or the airgap flow. Document steps to add host entries if necessary.

Telemetry and success metrics (local-first, privacy-preserving):
- Events file: ~/.quickprovision/events.log (each line JSON-lite, timestamp + event name)
- Probe events to record: quickprovision.init, quickprovision.up, example.generate.success, example.generate.failure, example.stream.started, example.stream.completed
- Success definition for onboarding: at least one example.generate.success within 15 minutes of init.

Airgap / customer POC packaging checklist
- Build container images with pinned digests (script: ./tools/build-airgap.sh)
- Tarball contents: images.tar.gz, runtime-binary, examples.tar.gz, README-offline.md
- Offline install flow: untar -> ./quickprovision --offline install -> quickprovision up --airgap
- Verify: examples run with REDWOOD_API_URL pointing at local host only (no external calls)

Guidelines for docs page (what to surface):
- Hero: "Get started in 10 minutes — no signup required" (link to ephemeral web demo)
- Two paths clearly signposted: Local dev loop (recommended) and ephemeral web demo
- Minimal troubleshooting section with the three top friction points above and exact commands to collect logs
- Quick checklist for evaluators and SREs at customer: ports, token location, confirm events.log entries

Open questions / design tradeoffs (to resolve in next sprint)
- Use docker-compose vs containerd-only: compose is more approachable, containerd aligns with infra. Decision: start with compose for wider compatibility, move to containerd later.
- Token UX: file vs ephemeral expiring token vs browser-based session. Which reduces support burden?
- Level of model fidelity: tiny shim model vs small-open quantized model. Shim reduces complexity; small model increases realism.

Action items (owners + rough due dates):
- Diego: prototype quickprovision init/up scripts (docker-compose) - target: 2024-12-05
- Priya: write examples for JS/Python and a minimal README page (landing doc + troubleshooting) - target: 2024-12-12
- Owen: telemetry spec and events.log schema (1-pager) - target: 2024-12-08
- Maya (me): consolidate doc, draft ephemeral web demo flow and PR for docs site - target: 2024-12-15

Unresolved tickets / links:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickprovision/pull/87 (proto init)
- CON-4121: doc request for airgap packaging spec
- Slack: #devexp-onboard thread starting 1703201234.000100 — contains UX feedback from field trials

Notes to self (scrappy, informal):
- Keep the quickstart tiny. If the first run takes >10m we lose momentum.
- Encourage reproducible failure: include a failing test that intentionally sends a malformed request to surface 400/422 handling.
- Use plain language on the README. The audience is busy engineers evaluating infra choices.

Appendix: minimal smoke test commands (to include in CI)
- curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8088/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/.quickprovision/token)" -d '{"model":"quick-demo","input":"Say hi in 1 sentence"}' | jq .
- curl -s http://localhost:8088/health | jq .
- node examples/js-hello/index.js  (should exit 0 and print text)

End of draft.
